title: Most Drivers Cannot Pass This Motorcycle Driving Test
summary: Explore Ready to Ride, Space and Control, Awareness and Balance, Surface and Visibility, Rider Judgment across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Think beyond the handlebars.
Test your road awareness.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: Ready to Ride, Space and Control, Awareness and Balance, Surface and Visibility, Rider Judgment. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. Not a licensing test or a substitute for professional rider training and local road rules.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

motorbike-q1.question: When is tyre pressure usually best checked for an accurate routine reading?

answers.a1: When the tyres are cold

motorbike-q2.question: Where should a rider generally direct their vision while travelling through a bend?

answers.a1: At the front wheel
answers.a2: Through the bend towards the intended path
answers.a3: At the edge of the road

motorbike-round1-new1.question: Where should the recommended tire pressure be obtained?

answers.a1: The motorcycle manufacturer's information
answers.a2: The highest number seen on another bike
answers.a4: The pressure used by every passenger car

motorbike-round1-new2.question: What should a rider do about a damaged or badly worn tire?

answers.a1: Have it assessed and replaced as appropriate before relying on it

motorbike-round1-new3.question: Why should lights be checked before a ride?

answers.a1: To help the rider see and be seen
answers.a3: To guarantee other drivers notice the bike
answers.a4: To compensate for all poor weather

motorbike-round1-new4.question: What is a sensible approach to entering an unfamiliar bend?

answers.a1: Choose an appropriate speed with room to respond to what becomes visible
answers.a2: Assume it has a constant radius
answers.a4: Focus only on the front wheel

motorbike-q3.question: Rain begins during a ride. What should happen to the space behind the vehicle ahead?

answers.a1: It should stay exactly the same
answers.a4: It matters only at high speed

motorbike-q4.question: On a modern motorcycle in a straight-line emergency stop, which broad technique is generally safest?

answers.a1: Use only the rear brake
answers.a2: Use only the front brake instantly
answers.a4: Apply both brakes progressively while keeping the motorcycle stable

motorbike-round2-new1.question: Why does following distance matter on a motorcycle?

answers.a1: It provides time and space to respond
answers.a2: It guarantees no one will brake
answers.a3: It removes the need to look ahead
answers.a4: It matters only at high speed

motorbike-round2-new2.question: What should a rider expect from wet metal covers or rails?

answers.a1: They may offer less grip than the surrounding road

motorbike-round2-new3.question: What can ABS help reduce during braking?

answers.a1: Wheel lock

motorbike-round2-new4.question: Why practise braking in approved training rather than learning only in an emergency?

answers.a1: Control skills benefit from supervised practice

motorbike-q5.question: Which habit best helps reduce the chance of another driver overlooking a motorcycle?

answers.a1: Stay out of blind spots and position for visibility
answers.a2: Ride beside a vehicle for as long as possible
answers.a3: Assume eye contact means the driver has seen you

motorbike-q6.question: What important change should a rider expect when carrying a passenger?

answers.a1: The motorcycle will turn and stop exactly the same
answers.a2: Balance, acceleration and braking distance may change
answers.a4: The passenger should lean opposite the rider

motorbike-round3-new1.question: What should a rider avoid assuming at a junction?

answers.a1: That another driver has seen them

motorbike-round3-new2.question: Why does protective clothing matter even on a short trip?

answers.a1: A fall can happen before much distance is covered

motorbike-round3-new3.question: What should a passenger receive before an unfamiliar ride?

answers.a1: Clear guidance consistent with the motorcycle and rider training
answers.a2: No information because riding is automatic

motorbike-round3-new4.question: Why check load limits when carrying luggage or a passenger?

answers.a1: Extra weight affects the machine and must stay within its limits
answers.a4: Loading removes the need for balance

motorbike-q7.question: How should a rider cross wet painted markings when they cannot be avoided?

answers.a1: Accelerate sharply while leaning
answers.a3: Keep the motorcycle as upright and smooth as possible

motorbike-q8.question: Before changing position into an area a mirror may not show, what final observation is valuable?

answers.a1: A glance at the speed display
answers.a2: A look at the front wheel
answers.a3: A check of the fuel level
answers.a4: A direct blind-spot check when it is safe

motorbike-round4-new1.question: What is a useful hazard-scanning habit?

answers.a1: Look ahead and keep updating the picture around you
answers.a2: Look only at the vehicle immediately ahead

motorbike-round4-new2.question: What does a mirror check not necessarily reveal?

answers.a1: Everything in a blind spot

motorbike-round4-new3.question: Why use smooth control inputs on reduced-grip surfaces?

answers.a1: Abrupt changes can challenge the available grip

motorbike-round4-new4.question: What should a rider do when visibility becomes too poor to continue safely?

answers.a1: Find a safe way to stop rather than outride visibility

motorbike-q9.question: Where should a rider find the correct drive-chain adjustment specification for their motorcycle?

answers.a1: The manufacturer's information
answers.a2: A guess based on another motorcycle

motorbike-q10.question: A rider notices their concentration fading on a long journey. What is the safest response?

answers.a1: Ride faster to finish sooner
answers.a2: Stop somewhere safe and take a proper break

motorbike-round5-new1.question: Why follow the maker's maintenance schedule?

answers.a1: Wear and adjustment needs depend on the motorcycle
It can reduce attention and reactions
answers.a4: It can be cured by speeding up

motorbike-round5-new3.question: What should a rider do if a medicine may cause drowsiness?

answers.a1: Check professional advice and avoid riding if impaired
answers.a2: Assume all prescribed medicines are safe for riding
answers.a3: Double the dose to finish sooner

motorbike-round5-new4.question: Which plan best handles a journey taking longer than expected?

answers.a1: Allow time for breaks and reassess conditions
answers.a2: Use speed to remove all delays
answers.a4: Treat the original schedule as a safety guarantee
